brief: One-and-a-half-storey frame cottage of 1860 on a city street: side-gabled, clapboard, a full-width front porch on slender posts, shuttered 6/6 windows and a centre door. Record: 1 photo plus 3 measured drawing sheets (plans, elevations, mantel and door details).

facade.notes: the H. Mould House (Cleveland, 1860): a small one-storey pyramid-roofed cottage with a recessed full porch, a central chimney, signs in the windows; a low iron fence along the sidewalk; crowded frame houses on both sides (a bargeboarded two-storey next door), wash lines and sheds in the back yards, a car in the drive; streetcar tracks in the street

why.note: the cheapest city cottage: a square box under a pyramid roof on a narrow lot
a 1930s inner-city block filtering down: crowded, worn, signs in the windows
